title: [10/12/2025] - Tea Leaves Processing into Five Tea Types
prompt: The diagram shows how tea leaves are processed into five tea types. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The diagram illustrates the process by which tea leaves are transformed into five different varieties of tea, namely white, green, oolong, large leaf black, and small leaf black tea.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, all five types of tea share the same initial and final stages, while the key differences lie in the intermediate steps, particularly in the fermentation and preparation methods. White tea undergoes the simplest process, whereas the two varieties of black tea require the most extensive processing, including full fermentation.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: The production of all tea types begins with leaf growth, followed by plucking and wilting, also known as withering. At this point, the process diverges depending on the type of tea being produced. For white tea, the leaves proceed directly to oven drying without any additional treatment, making it the most straightforward variety to produce. Green tea, by contrast, requires two extra steps: the wilted leaves are first steamed and then rolled before being dried in the oven.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: The remaining three varieties all involve fermentation. For oolong tea, after wilting, the leaves are rolled and undergo slight fermentation before the final drying stage. The two black tea types follow a similar path but with full fermentation instead. The primary distinction between large leaf and small leaf black tea lies in their preparation method: while large leaf black tea is produced through rolling, small leaf black tea uses crushing to break down the leaves before fermentation and drying.
